assumptions: Cases are offline contract and quality specifications; browser research requires a separately authorized live run.
The procedure writes one Markdown artifact under reports/earned-media/<run_id>.md and has no outbound side effects.
The agent must use current source dates and reject unsupported or promotional opportunities instead of manufacturing a result.
cost_drivers: One bounded browser-backed Codex session uses the existing pinned model pricing and spending ceiling; no managed-model routes are declared.
Research effort varies with company-site clarity, candidate count and source accessibility; the procedure is bounded to eight candidates and a 900-second run.
Public web traffic and browser infrastructure costs are separate from Tin model accounting.
effects: Read-only public HTTPS pages through the browser sandbox.
One run-owned Markdown artifact in project state.
No email, publication, journalist contact, website edit, project-file edit, provider mutation or recursive workflow start.

rubric.question: Does the opportunity distinguish news evidence from company evidence and avoid unsupported claims?
Does the opportunity enforce the configured recency window using an actual source date or honestly report missing precision?
Does the hook add a specific information gap or analysis rather than generic commentary?
When no candidate passes the gates or threshold, does the report clearly refuse to manufacture an opportunity?

cases.description: A normal run should produce one evidence-backed brief after current-story discovery.

inputs.expertise: authentication anomaly detection and incident response
inputs.company_evidence: The company publishes documented incident-response guidance and maintains an anonymized annual anomaly report.

cases.description: A supplied story is analyzed as the primary candidate without requiring broad discovery.
Stale, irrelevant, generic or unsupported candidates must result in an honest no-opportunity decision.
